feedback.answered: The legal RawNode overlap was reached. Control automatically left joint at index 6. Overlap discarded one emitted TimeoutNow, completed the joint entry at index 5, timed out transfer, and remained leader in term 2 with applied=committed=last=5 and AutoLeave=true after 30 ticks. All queue and Ready work was drained. A separately labeled ordinary proposal then caused automatic exit and application through index 7. These are exploration observations, not formal property Evidence.

question.question: Does automatic joint-configuration exit retain an implementation-owned continuation when the application-completion attempt is rejected during leadership transfer and the transfer later times out with the same leader, a live joint quorum, and no unrelated proposals?
question.importance: A joint configuration can remain effective after the requested implicit transition should finalize, continuing to require the outgoing quorum and preventing ordinary subsequent membership changes. This is a scoped membership progress responsibility, not a demonstrated consensus safety violation.

question.trigger_rationale: Execution 861953bdd0e545bf959d3d4cf9b1c090 reached the overlap through real RawNode operations: after timeout and 30 ticks, applied=committed=last=5, AutoLeave=true, transferee=0, no Ready or queued message. A diagnostic new proposal led to exit at index 7. Source traces show application completion is the retry trigger and timeout only clears transfer. Register the automatic continuation obligation, then fix a recurrence-based check; do not recast exploratory output as formal evidence.

obligation.description: For an applied implicit-joint configuration with automatic exit enabled, Raft must retain or re-establish its own continuation to propose and complete safe exit after an overlapping leadership transfer fails, when an eligible leader and both required quorums remain available and the caller continues required ticking, message delivery, persistence and application. Completion must not depend on an unrelated new caller proposal or a caller-supplied explicit leave-joint change.

scope.description: Automatic membership-finalization responsibility after transfer rejection of the application-triggered exit attempt. Stable current leader remains a voter; configuration is committed and applied, transfer is no longer pending, and reliable delivery resumes after loss of the transfer request. No numeric completion deadline is asserted.
assumptions: Non-Byzantine nodes and permitted network message loss followed by reliable delivery.
Caller processes every Ready with persistence and in-order application, calls Advance, ticks all nodes, and applies each committed configuration entry exactly once.
A current-term entry is already committed and the implicit configuration itself has completed application.
excluded: Explicit joint mode, where the caller owns the exit proposal.
Permanent communication/storage failures or leader removal.
Global client endpoints and numerical response-time guarantees.

grounding.derivation: The public ConfChangeTransitionJointImplicit contract assigns automatic exit by proposing a zero configuration change to Raft; ConfState.AutoLeave specifies finalization when safe. EnterJoint implements that selection. appliedTo explicitly acknowledges rejection during transfer and describes retry on later advance. The general caller-retry contract for dropped Propose/ProposeConfChange calls does not transfer ownership of this library-generated exit to the caller, especially because JointExplicit separately exposes that choice. The requirement concerns eventual implementation-owned continuation under continuing duties, not completion within an invented tick bound.
grounding.applicability: Implicit-joint change already committed/applied, same eligible leader remains, transfer timeout removes the temporary proposal-rejection guard, and both quorums and caller services remain available.
alternatives: Later unrelated proposal or leadership replacement can rescue progress; these are not required caller steps under the selected implicit-joint interface.

formation.explanation: Node serializes incoming proposals, ticks and messages, or caller serializes RawNode. A leader assigns term/index and emits replication. Followers match predecessor history and defer positive append support until persistence. Leader self support also waits for storage. Match values are aggregated over incoming and, if joint, outgoing majority; commitment requires the selected index to belong to the current term. Appends propagate commit and heartbeats bound it by the recipient Match. Ready delivers committed history; applying and applied remain distinct until caller completion.

context.explanation: Eligible voters campaign only after committed configuration work is applied. Real elections increment term and record durable votes; pre-vote probes without incrementing local term. Log freshness and voter quorums qualify authority. Higher-term ordinary traffic steps down; lower-term traffic is generally discarded. Candidate accepts only its current vote phase. Leader transfer pauses proposals until target catches up and TimeoutNow starts a forced election; timeout aborts transfer. Quorum loss can step down. Membership application changes voter eligibility and may remove the leader.

connection.explanation: Term/role and installed configuration determine which support the leader consumes. Reset discards vote tallies, remote Match estimates and acknowledged read queue but preserves log/commit history; new leaders append a current-term no-op, and log freshness carries committed history through elections. Old-term append support is ignored. Old storage completions cannot stabilize overwritten entries, while snapshot/application completions concern already decided history and remain meaningful across terms. Restoration reconstructs history and configuration before eligibility. Pending pre-commit reads are a distinct queue whose lifetime needs investigation. Membership updates may recompute commit, whereas application completion can propose automatic joint exit; these follow-up effects are not interchangeable.

formation.explanation: Node serializes incoming proposals, ticks and messages, or caller serializes RawNode. A leader assigns term/index and emits replication. Followers match predecessor history and defer positive append support until persistence. Leader self support also waits for storage. Match values are aggregated over incoming and, if joint, outgoing majority; commitment requires the selected index to belong to the current term. Appends propagate commit and heartbeats bound it by the recipient Match. Ready delivers committed history; applying and applied remain distinct until caller completion.

context.explanation: Eligible voters campaign only after committed configuration work is applied. Real elections increment term and record durable votes; pre-vote probes without incrementing local term. Log freshness and voter quorums qualify authority. Higher-term ordinary traffic steps down; lower-term traffic is generally discarded. Candidate accepts only its current vote phase. Leader transfer pauses proposals until target catches up and TimeoutNow starts a forced election; timeout aborts transfer. Quorum loss can step down. Membership application changes voter eligibility and may remove the leader.

connection.explanation: Term/role and installed configuration determine which support the leader consumes. Reset discards vote tallies, remote Match estimates and acknowledged read queue but preserves log/commit history; new leaders append a current-term no-op, and log freshness carries committed history through elections. Old-term append support is ignored. Old storage completions cannot stabilize overwritten entries, while snapshot/application completions concern already decided history and remain meaningful across terms. Restoration reconstructs history and configuration before eligibility. Pending pre-commit reads are a distinct queue whose lifetime needs investigation. Membership updates may recompute commit, whereas application completion can propose automatic joint exit; these follow-up effects are not interchangeable.

Actual legal overlap and ordinary heartbeat/Ready behavior are the remaining construction uncertainty. The alternative queued-read discrepancy has a stronger reachability guard (campaign blocks unapplied committed configuration); this smaller continuation exploration is presently more discriminating.

Sourced implicit-joint contract grounds automatic finalization; the exploration reaches the disputed overlap and justifies a separately fixed continuation check without imposing an arbitrary deadline.

feedback.answered: The legal RawNode overlap was reached. Control automatically left joint at index 6. Overlap discarded one emitted TimeoutNow, completed the joint entry at index 5, timed out transfer, and remained leader in term 2 with applied=committed=last=5 and AutoLeave=true after 30 ticks. All queue and Ready work was drained. A separately labeled ordinary proposal then caused automatic exit and application through index 7. These are exploration observations, not formal property Evidence.
